proof:
# Exact k-fold expansion and a nested-residue invariant

Let d>=1,n>=0, let k>=1 be an integer, and let A be a nonempty bounded compact subset of (p+kZ^n) x R^d. Put

a=vol_MI(A), b=max_z vol_d(A_z),
G=(A+...+A)/k,

where the sum has k copies. Then

vol_MI(G)>=k a-(k-1)b.

## Proof

Every integer-coordinate index of G is integral: the sum of k source indices p+kz_i divided by k is p+sum z_i. Write a_z=vol_d(A_z), g_m=vol_d(G_m). For positive-volume source fibers, the k-fold continuous Brunn-Minkowski inequality gives

g_{(z_1+...+z_k)/k}
>= [(a_{z_1}^{1/d}+...+a_{z_k}^{1/d})/k]^d
>=min_i a_{z_i}.

For t>0 put Z_t={z:a_z>=t}. For nonempty Z_t,

#{m:g_m>=t} >= |kZ_t| >= k|Z_t|-k+1.

Here kZ_t denotes the k-fold Minkowski sum. The finite-set sum bound |U+V|>=|U|+|V|-1 follows by ordering U and V with a common generic linear functional and taking a monotone path of sum indices; its functional values strictly increase. Induction on k gives the displayed k-fold bound. When n=0 every nonempty Z_t is a singleton and the bound holds directly.

Integrate over 0<t<=b. Finite layer-cake summation gives

sum_m g_m >= integral_0^b (k|Z_t|-k+1)dt
=k sum_z a_z-(k-1)b.

If a=0, then b=0 and the assertion is trivial. This also explains why zero-volume source fibers cause no issue: they do not occur in any positive level set.

## Sharpness

For n>=1 let A have identical convex d-dimensional fiber K of volume v over

0,k e_1,2k e_1,...,(N-1)k e_1.

Then G has exactly the identical fibers K over j e_1, j=0,...,k(N-1). Thus its mixed volume is [k(N-1)+1]v=k Nv-(k-1)v, giving equality. For n=0, one convex fiber gives equality as well.

## Extension to an exclusive convex cap region

Let Q be a bounded Borel convex subset of ambient space, possibly nonclosed, and put E=Q intersect Lambda. For a residue class p+kZ^n write

a_p=vol_MI(E intersect ((p+kZ^n) x R^d)),
b_p=max_{z in p+kZ^n} vol_d(E_z),

with b_p=0 if the class has no positive-volume fiber. Then

vol_MI(E)>=k a_p-(k-1)b_p.

To prove this when Q is nonclosed, choose compact subsets of its finitely many class fibers whose total volume tends to a_p. Their union A is compact and lies in Q and the residue class. Convexity places its k-fold average in Q, and divisibility places that average in Lambda. Its largest fiber volume is at most b_p. Apply the proved compact inequality and let the compact approximations exhaust the class volume. This uses only ordinary inner regularity of finite Lebesgue measure in each fiber.

An exclusive cap region of the form C intersect H_i intersect intersection_{j!=i} H_j^c is convex and Borel even though some inequalities are strict. Therefore this extension applies to it exactly, without silently replacing open sides by closed sides.

Equivalently, class dispersion obeys

a_p-b_p <= [vol_MI(E)-b_p]/k.

## A genuine nested-residue telescope

Fix nested residue classes p_r+2^r Z^n, r=0,1,..., with each contained in its predecessor, and set

A_r=E intersect ((p_r+2^r Z^n) x R^d),
a_r=vol_MI(A_r), b_r=maxfiber(A_r).

The midpoint average of A_r lies in A_{r-1}: both source indices have the same class modulo 2^r, so their midpoint has the parent class modulo 2^{r-1}; convexity keeps it in Q. The compact-approximation argument therefore gives

a_{r-1}>=2a_r-b_r.

Define

Phi_0=a_0,
Phi_r=2^r a_r-sum_{j=1}^r 2^{j-1}b_j.

Multiplying the one-step inequality by 2^{r-1} shows Phi_r<=Phi_{r-1}. Hence

2^r a_r <= a_0+sum_{j=1}^r 2^{j-1}b_j.

This invariant is independent of the number 2^n of children of a residue class. It retains an essential correction at each scale for the largest remaining fiber. It does not assert that a favorable residue path exists, that different class averages are disjoint, or that any class contains an OC center.

If b_r is bounded above by a common B, the telescope yields a_r<=B+(a_0-B)/2^r. Direct application of the k=2^r theorem with the final-class maximum b_r can be sharper than this common-B estimate.
